short_description: NAMI is a US nonprofit offering a free peer-staffed HelpLine, local support groups and peer-taught classes such as Family-to-Family.
long_description: The National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI) is a US nonprofit with a national office and local affiliates. Its HelpLine (1-800-950-6264, or text "NAMI" to 62640) is free and confidential and gives information, resource referrals and support to people with mental health conditions, families and caregivers, Monday to Friday, 10 a.m. to 10 p.m. ET, with specialty lines for family caregivers, teens and young adults, and Spanish speakers; it is not a crisis line and refers crises to 988. Local affiliates run free support groups and peer-taught classes, including Family-to-Family for relatives of people with mental illness. NAMI provides education and peer support, not clinical treatment. Family-to-Family has been tested in a randomized trial of 318 family members in Maryland, where participants gained more knowledge, coping and empowerment and had less anxiety than a waitlist group at three months, with gains sustained at nine months.

sections.title: About NAMI
sections.text: The National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI) is the nation's largest grassroots mental health organization. Founded in 1979, NAMI is dedicated to building better lives for the millions of Americans affected by mental illness. With over 600 local affiliates across the country, NAMI provides education, support, and advocacy to people with mental health conditions and their families. The organization emphasizes that mental health conditions are medical conditions that deserve the same treatment and support as physical health conditions.

sections.title: NAMI HelpLine
sections.text: The NAMI HelpLine (1-800-950-NAMI) is a free, nationwide peer-support service providing information, resource referrals, and support to people living with mental health conditions, their family members, caregivers, and the general public. The HelpLine is staffed by trained volunteers and staff with lived experience. Services include answering questions about mental health conditions, finding treatment providers, navigating insurance, and connecting to support groups and programs.

sections.title: NAMI Programs
sections.text: NAMI offers free evidence-based educational programs including Family-to-Family (an 8-session course for families and caregivers), Peer-to-Peer (for adults living with mental health conditions), NAMI Basics (for parents and caregivers of children), and Homefront (for military families). These programs are taught by trained peers who have personal experience with mental illness. NAMI also runs thousands of support groups nationwide where people can share experiences in a safe environment.

sections.title: Find Your Local NAMI
sections.text: NAMI has over 600 local affiliates across the United States, each providing programs and services tailored to their community. Local affiliates offer in-person support groups, educational classes, community outreach, and connections to local mental health resources. To find your local NAMI affiliate, visit nami.org and enter your zip code. Local affiliates are often staffed by volunteers with personal experience with mental illness who can provide peer support and guidance.

pricing.notes: HelpLine, support groups and NAMI education programs are free; standard text message and data rates may apply.

privacy.notes: Website policy (2020) says NAMI does not sell donor information or share personal information with unrelated third parties; it uses Google Analytics, and full account deletion requires contacting NAMI. The policy does not mention HIPAA.

faqs.a: Yes, all NAMI programs, classes, and support groups are free. NAMI is a nonprofit funded by donations. You can attend Family-to-Family classes, Peer-to-Peer groups, and support meetings at no cost.

Family-to-Family is a free 8-week education class for family members and caregivers of people with mental illness. It covers diagnosis, treatment, coping strategies, and self-care. Classes are taught by trained family members who've been there.

No, NAMI provides education and peer support, not clinical treatment. NAMI support groups are led by people with lived experience, not therapists. For therapy, use NAMI's HelpLine to find treatment resources in your area.

faqs.q: How do I find my local NAMI?
faqs.a: Visit nami.org and search for your local NAMI affiliate. There are NAMI chapters throughout the US offering in-person and virtual programs. The NAMI HelpLine (1-800-950-NAMI) can also connect you with local resources.

patient_summary: You can call 1-800-950-6264 or text "NAMI" to 62640 on weekdays to talk to a trained peer about resources and next steps, or join a free local support group or class through your NAMI affiliate. Everything is free. NAMI is peer support and education, not therapy, and it is not a crisis line.
